text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGERS: KV prefix cache error spike detected on us-west1 serving cluster — elevated evictions and batching backlog. Root TS 1895007654. Auto-notify sent to #incidents and on-call.
Alex M.: seeing continuous batch backlog on a few GPU pools, memory on kv-store node spiking to 94%.
Priya S.: paging oncall — this looks like prompt-prefix key churn. Rate of new prompt hashes exploded around 00:12 UTC.
Samir K.: confirmed — tokenizer changes from the nightly model deploy (tokenizer_v2) created a mismatch for template normalization. Hashes don't line up, so cache misses -> cache population storm.
Dana R.: customer impact? any 5xxs or latency SLO breaches?
Alex M.: small subset of customers hitting 503s from the short-circuit when cache thrash causes the front-end to hit fallback path. Latency p95 jumped from 120ms -> 850ms for affected routes. Roughly 3-4% of total requests in us-west in the last 15m.
Priya S.: INC-2026-45 created. brief: prefix cache invalidation bug post-tokenizer update -> continuous batching regression -> kv blowup.
Samir K.: mitigation plan: 1) disable continuous batching for affected model variant 2) throttle new prefix writes to KV 3) roll back tokenizer change on serving nodes if needed.
Alex M.: rolling a hotfix: set continuous_batching.enabled=false for model-family=rlm-13b in us-west1. Applying as canary to 2 nodes first.
ops-bot: deploy job queued: deploy/hotfix/disable-cont-batching -> canary on nodes gpool-usw-4a, gpool-usw-4b (ID #df3b9).
Priya S.: I'm on the rollback path if canary fails. Notifying support leads to prepare CS message template.
Dana R.: tagging affected customers: accounts with heavy prompt-template usage and long prefixes. We'll need targeted outreach if outage expands.
Alex M.: canary applied. Observing immediate drop in KV write rate, evictions stabilizing. Latency decreasing.
Samir K.: running kv-store eviction diagnostic: write rate down 82% after disabling continuous batching on canary nodes. Nice.
Priya S.: escalate to full cluster apply? risk of increased per-request latency for other small requests due to disabled batching. tradeoff is stability.
Dana R.: agree do full apply in 3 minutes if canary stays green. I'll draft customer-facing note just in case.
Alex M.: full apply started at 00:39 UTC. patch: 
```\n# hotfix\nmodel_selector: rlm-13b\ncontinuous_batching:\n  enabled: false\n  batch_window_ms: 0\n```\napply command: /infra apply --cluster usw --selector rlm-13b --patch hotfix-disable-cont-batching
ops-bot: apply completed on 12 nodes. job id df3b9 -> df3b9-rc2.
Samir K.: post-apply metrics: KV write QPS back to baseline, memory usage slipping down to 62%, p95 latency back to ~140ms. Errors reduced to baseline.
Priya S.: rolling TTL change to reduce cache churn risk: increase prefix cache TTL from 30s -> 5m on a staged basis. This reduces regen storms while we patch tokenizer mismatch.
Alex M.: starting controlled TTL increase for prefix cache: /kvctl set-ttl --prefix-prefix --ttl 300 --cluster usw --selector rlm-13b
Dana R.: support note ready: short blurb describing transient elevated latency and 503s affecting small percentage of us-west customers; engineers mitigated by toggling batching and increasing prefix TTL. CS contact: cs-ops@redwood.com.
Priya S.: tokenizer rollback plan: we can either re-deploy tokenizer_v1 normalization or update hashing pipeline to canonicalize tokens across v1/v2. Prefer canonicalization but that's a longer fix. Rollback deployed if instability returns.
Samir K.: starting a short audit of prompt templates to identify most-churned prefixes. We'll create an exclusion list to avoid caching highly volatile prefixes.
Dana R.: any data loss or degraded quality? customers reported duplicate tokens in outputs?
Alex M.: no data loss. Some prefix collisions caused slightly inconsistent completions for a handful of sessions; we'll follow up.
Priya S.: handoff to next oncall (Dana) in 40 minutes. Documenting follow-ups:
- Owner: Samir K. -> investigate tokenizer/hash canonicalization (ticket ENGINF-3383).
- Owner: Alex M. -> postmortem + rollout notes (PM: Priya).
- Owner: Dana R. -> customer comms and tracking (INC-2026-45).
ops-bot: reminder: set SLA override and extend trace retention for the incident for 48h.
Dana R.: taking handoff. Current status: mitigations applied (continuous batching disabled, TTL extended), customer impact contained (~3% requests briefly). Next steps: monitor for 2 more hours, run load test against patched config, and prioritize canonical tokenizer/hash fix.
Priya S.: will open a targeted perf regression eval for our nightly tokenization change to prevent this class of regressions. Adding automated alert when prefix write QPS > 2x baseline for 10m.
Samir K.: quick note: add a small circuit-breaker that temporarily rejects new prefix writes if KV write queue depth > threshold. That would prevent self-amplifying cache storms. Filing ENGINF-3384.
Alex M.: thanks all. I'll start the postmortem draft. Please add any logs or traces you grabbed to INC-2026-45.
Dana R.: leaving this channel but monitoring. ping me if we need to roll tokenizer back. :phone: :white_check_mark:
